items.title: Over 40% Group A posts vacant at PGIMS Rohtak, says former Minister
points: Alleging that 41.6% of the sanctioned Group A posts at the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGIMS) in Rohtak were lying vacant, former Haryana Home Minister Subhash Batra on Sunday questioned the BJP government’s claims of improving healthcare…
Citing an inspection by the Assembly’s Subject Committee in February, Mr. Batra said 424 of the 1,018 sanctioned Group A posts at the institute were vacant.
He said the shortage of doctors, specialists and healthcare staff was affecting patient care at the institute, which catered to over 8,000 patients daily in its outpatient department.
Manjunath, in-charge of the Public Relations Department, PGIMS, did not respond to repeated calls and messages seeking his response to the former Minister’s allegations.

Addressing a press conference, Mr. Batra also pointed out that only 200 of the 540 medicines on the government-approved list were available in the hospital store during the Health Minister’s inspection in April.
Supply orders for 172 types of medicines and surgical materials were pending with companies, he alleged.

items.title: CM Vijay to hold meeting with MLAs of allies, supporting parties
points: Joseph Vijay is set to hold a meeting with MLAs of alliance partners and parties extending outside support to his government on Monday (November 23).
According to sources, the meeting is scheduled to take place at 3 p.m. on Monday at Pamani Illam, the Chief Minister’s Camp Office on Greenways Road in Chennai.
During the meeting, Mr. Vijay is expected to discuss with MLAs from alliance partners such as the Congress, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi, and the Indian Union Muslim League.
MLAs of the Left parties extending outside support to Mr. Vijay’s government are also likely to take part.

Sources said that the meeting would focus on the implementation of infrastructure and welfare measures in their constituencies, and each MLA had been asked to present their constituency-related demands to the Chief Minister.

The proposed meeting assumes significance against the backdrop of the TVK-led coalition government completing six months in office recently, and the impending byelections to six Assembly constituencies.

items.title: Kasimedu fisherfolk withdraw strike after Minister’s intervention
points: Fishermen of Kasimedu on Sunday withdrew their indefinite strike, seeking the release of eight boats impounded by the Andhra Pradesh government, after the intervention of Finance Minister N.
Marie Wilson, who is also the MLA for Dr. Radhakrishnan Nagar Assembly constituency.
The Minister, who reached the fishing harbour on Sunday morning, interacted with the leaders of various associations, and listened to their grievances for about an hour.
The fisherfolk had also demanded that the State government increase the solatium paid to the kin of fishermen who died in Cyclone Murasu.
Mr. Marie Wilson said he had taken up their issues with Chief Minister C.
Joseph Vijay, and that steps would be taken to increase the compensation and bring the boats back.
A former Fisheries Department official said the boats had been impounded in Andhra Pradesh since April, without the relevant provisions of the Marine Fisheries Regulation Act being implemented.

Inspector Manjith Lal was suspended by District Police Chief (Kochi City) R.

The inspector also allegedly shared details of the Indian Cooperative Credit Society Ltd and its key officials with Mr. Vellappalath at his request.

He recently endorsed maintaining strong ties with Israel, citing India's defence requirements and national interests, while condemning both the October 7 Hamas attacks on Israel and the Benjamin Netanyahu-led government's subsequent military offensive in…

items.title: Bag With Rs 55-Lakh Gold Jewellery Swapped In Delhi Recovered From Bengaluru
points: A bag containing gold jewellery worth Rs 55 lakh, along with some cash that was accidentally swapped in Delhi's ISBT Kashmiri Gate, was traced and recovered within a few days from Bengaluru.

The incident began on November 12, when the complainant, Amrit Raj Verma, reported that his black backpack had gone missing near the baggage checking machine at the entrance on the first floor of the ISBT Kashmiri Gate terminal.
The bag contained clothing, approximately Rs 9,000 in cash, a mobile charger, an Aadhaar card, and gold jewellery valued at around Rs 55 lakh.
During the investigation, a lead regarding the movements of a suspect emerged, tracing back to a bus journey that originated in Bengaluru.
The police scrutinised various financial transactions, including a payment of Rs 174 linked to a Bengaluru bus depot and subsequent Paytm transactions, which provided crucial leads.
Following persistent technical surveillance, a detailed review of CCTV footage, and an intensive search, the police team successfully located the individual on November 18.

items.title: MPs Who Broke Away From Mamata Banerjee Expand Their Party NCPI Into Rural Bengal
points: Thirteen gram panchayats and two panchayat samitis in North 24 Parganas have left the Trinamool Congress (TMC) and joined the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), the party that 20 of 28 TMC MPs joined some months after breaking away following…
The NCPI, which has backed the BJP-led NDA, is now extending its reach from Parliament into Bengal's rural local bodies.
The Sandeshkhali-I and Minakhan panchayat samitis in Basirhat Lok Sabha segment, both previously under TMC control, are among the bodies that have switched sides.
The defection of 20 TMC Lok Sabha MPs to the NCPI earlier this year made the little-known party the second-largest constituent of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA).
The Lok Sabha segment has been vacant since September 2024, following the death of Trinamool MP Haji Nurul Islam.

The Election Commission has not scheduled a by-election because an election petition challenging his 2024 victory remains pending in the Calcutta High Court There, the NCPI has taken control of one gram panchayat and panchayat samiti after another.

items.title: YS Sharmila Stopped From Visiting Brother Jagan Reddy's Bengaluru Home
points: Andhra Pradesh Congress chief and YS Jaganmohan Reddy's sister YS Sharmila was stopped by the Bengaluru police near Kempegowda International Airport when she tried to visit the disputed Yelahanka bungalow.
The bungalow is where the former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister's family resides.

Sharmila, accompanied by her mother YS Vijayamma and other family members, was prevented from proceeding towards the property following an interim injunction issued by a Devanahalli court on November 21.
The order restrains Sharmila and her representatives from entering or interfering with the property.

The dispute comes amid a family feud over property rights and arrangements for Sharmila's daughter's November 25 wedding, which was initially planned at their Bengaluru residence but later shifted to Hyderabad.
Jagan Reddy and YS Sharmila have had a long-standing property dispute.

Reddy had written to the National Company Law Tribunal or NCLT, seeking to nullify her "illegal' transfer of shares in Saraswati Power and Industries Private Limited to herself and their mother YS Vijayalakshmi.

items.title: Driver Asleep, Car Crashes Into Kerala Library. Crowd Escapes Narrowly
points: A group of passengers waiting for a bus, including a woman carrying a child, escaped miraculously from what could have been a serious accident after a speeding car crashed into a library building at Mannurkonam near Nedumangad in Kerala.
The accident occurred around 1:54 pm on the Mannur-Vithura road, near the People's Library at Mannurkonam Junction.

According to preliminary information, the car, travelling at high speed from the Chullimanoor side, veered off the road and crashed into the library building, narrowly missing four passengers standing nearby.
A brown-coloured Wagon R suddenly speeds towards them after losing control, almost crashing into the people standing near the library.
The crowd barely manages to escape when the car crashes into the building.
The driver, identified as Anil Kumar (56), a resident of Ponmudi, is believed to have fallen asleep at the wheel, leading to the accident.
She received treatment at the Nedumangad District Hospital.
The impact damaged a pillar of the People's Library building, which was constructed in 1982.

items.title: Hyderabad Police issue alert over terror threat email; security checks conducted at key locations

The sender also threatened to replicate the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks in Hyderabad.
In case of noticing any suspicious person or unattended object, the public is requested to immediately inform the police by dialling 112.

The sender allegedly threatened to carry out bomb blasts at the two locations, claiming that the attacks were intended to kill at least 300 people.

“The sender further threatened to replicate the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks in Hyderabad on the same day, stating that the attacks were intended to avenge the killing of their leader Lateef Bhat and other associates by the Indian Army,” the alert message said.

items.title: San Pedro Bay Ports Mark 20 Years of Landmark Clean Air Action Plan
points: Twenty years after adopting the landmark Clean Air Action Plan (CAAP), the ports of Long Beach and Los Angeles are advancing a new phase of clean air initiatives, building on two decades of dramatic reductions in air pollution while accelerating the…
20, 2006, the CAAP established a coordinated strategy to reduce air pollution from ships, trucks, trains, cargo-handling equipment and harbor craft.

Since 2005, combined port-related emissions of diesel particulate matter have fallen 90%, nitrogen oxides 70% and sulfur oxides 98%, even as the ports have handled growing volumes of international trade.
“The Clean Air Action Plan is an amazing story of collaboration, innovation and persistence.

“What began here 20 years ago has transformed the San Pedro Bay ports complex and reverberated across our industry, all while we experience the busiest years in our history,” said Port of Long Beach CEO Dr. Noel Hacegaba.

items.title: Barclays warns of further equity weakness as hawkish Fed bets build
points: Equities could weaken further into year-end if Federal Reserve communication turns more hawkish or inflation data comes in hot, as investors question whether the central bank’s support has disappeared, according to Barclays.
Strategists led by Emmanuel Cau said the “bigger challenge for equities is the perception that the Fed put has disappeared,” beyond recent volatility in AI-linked stocks.
Strong growth and sticky inflation have driven a sharp repricing of rate expectations, they said.
Barclays compared the situation with December 2018, when equities fell about 20% before the Fed pivoted to a more dovish stance and stocks rallied sharply in early 2019.
Markets now fully price a December rate increase, and comments by Fed Governor Christopher Waller have fueled some speculation of a 50 basis point move.
Barclays economists disagree, arguing such a step would signal panic and imply that October’s pause was a mistake.

items.title: ECB to expand currency swap lines, Lagarde says
points: The European Central Bank plans to make its currency swap lines with other countries more accessible to protect the euro area from external financial shocks and strengthen the euro’s global position, ECB President Christine Lagarde said.
The ECB currently maintains swap lines only with major central banks including the US Federal Reserve and the People’s Bank of China.

Lagarde’s remarks indicate these financial tools may eventually become available to a broader range of countries as the ECB works to increase international use of the euro and reduce the euro zone’s reliance on the US dollar for trade and investment.
“We are working to keep our swap lines fit for purpose in a more fragmented world,” Lagarde told a conference.

“They will be more accessible, too.” Policymakers worldwide have raised questions about the dollar’s long-term dominance given U.S. President Donald Trump’s unpredictable economic policy and the United States’ growing public debt.

items.title: Fed’s Paulson open to back-to-back rate hikes at steady pace
points: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said today she would consider consecutive interest-rate increases at upcoming policy meetings to address inflation, while emphasizing the need for a measured approach.
“The direction of travel, in terms of where rates need to go, is really clear,” Paulson said today in an interview with Bloomberg News in New York.
“They need to be higher.” Paulson said she favored moving in a “deliberate way” to give households, businesses and banks more time to adjust.
The Fed raised its benchmark rate by a quarter percentage point to a range of 3.75% to 4% in September, then held steady last month.
Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack has advocated for small but successive increases.
The Philadelphia Fed chief votes on monetary policy this year but not in 2027.
Investors expect rate increases in December and January, though the odds of the latter have declined amid sharp drops in equity markets driven by technology stocks.

items.title: Eight killed as speeding minivan rams into roadside tree in Tamil Nadu's Tiruchirappalli
points: Eight people were killed and two others injured after a minivan lost control and rammed into a roadside tree in Tamil Nadu's Tiruchirappalli district on Sunday, police said.
The incident took place at around 4 pm in Musiri, which is located about 350 km south of Chennai, an officer said.

The minivan, a Maruti EECO, was carrying 10 passengers who were returning to Thirukattupalli in Thanjavur district after taking part in a relative's ear piercing function in Namakkal, investigating officers said.
Preliminary investigation revealed that the driver of the van, identified as Rajesh, lost control of the vehicle due to overspeeding, following which it collided into a tree.
Five passengers – Manickam, Sangili, Murugan, Pavadaidied and the vehicle driver Rajesh – died on the spot, Jembunathapuram police officials told HT.
The other five passengers, who had sustained severe injuries, were rushed to the Musiri Government Hospital for treatment.
However, three among them – identified as Sakthivel, Subramani, and Seetharaman – succumbed to their injuries at the medical facility.

items.title: Parliament On Hold, Delimitation Hangs Between BJP's 3-Day Plan, Congress' 4 Demands
points: It's been a record 100 days since Parliament's Monsoon Session last sat, and it still hasn't been prorogued or formally concluded, amid increasing chatter that the Narendra Modi government still has a plan up its sleeve to avenge a defeat.
The 100-day gap is the longest so far in India's parliamentary history, having beaten the previous record of 87 days from 2008.

The government is learnt to be using the time to work towards the two-thirds majority that it needs to pass the delimitation bill, which it has linked to operationalising the reservation of 33 per cent of seats in Parliament and state legislatures for women.
The Congress, which has said the quota as granted by a 2023 law should be delinked from census and delimitation, has set out roughly four conditions.
The third is that the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, the women's reservation law of 2023, be put into effect, with 182 of the existing 543 seats reserved for women.

Kantarao, treasurer of the organisation, said the government had not said how many jobs would be created, even as data centre capacity rose to over six gigawatts.

items.title: Hyderabad on high alert after email from ‘LeT operatives’ warns of terror attacks
points: Hyderabad police went on high alert on Sunday following input from the Special Branch, which received a threatening email warning of terror attacks in the city, officials said.

The email, reportedly sent in the name of Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), identified Kachiguda Railway Station and Hotel Tourist Plaza as potential targets for bomb explosions, similar to the Mumbai terror attacks of November 26, 2008.
The email warned of attacks in retaliation for the killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba commander and most-wanted terrorist Lateef Bhatt and his associates by the Indian Army in Jammu and Kashmir.
It also threatened multiple attacks in Hyderabad, claiming that at least 300 people would be killed.
The Special Branch police directed the city’s security agencies to intensify surveillance and take precautionary measures to prevent any untoward incident.
Kachiguda Railway Station and Hotel Tourist Plaza have been specifically identified in the threat, prompting authorities to strengthen security at these locations.

items.title: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri International, flags ‘unsafe packaged drinking water’
points: Food regulator FSSAI on Sunday said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after finding its sample of packaged drinking water "unsafe".
In a social media post, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd regarding "unsafe packaged drinking water".
A regulatory sample of "Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)" was collected from the premises of Bisleri International for analysis.
"The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator said.
Upon appeal by the company, the sample was sent to the referral food laboratory, which also declared it "unsafe" due to the detection of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator added.
The findings of the lab established violations relating to unsafe food under the law.

items.title: Taiwan Mulls Lowering Margin Requirement to Support Stock Market
points: Taiwan is considering lowering the margin requirement ratio for stock investors using borrowed funds as it tries to stem a selloff after the benchmark equity index’s worst week in 35 years.

The Taiwan Stock Exchange said it held an emergency meeting with 10 local brokerages Sunday to discuss the potential move, which would cut the minimum margin maintenance ratio to 120% from the current 130%.

Taiwan currently requires a minimum margin maintenance ratio of 130% for investors who buy stocks with borrowed funds, meaning the market value of their securities must remain at least 1.3 times the amount borrowed.
Authorities also raised the minimum margin requirement for short sales to 150% from 130%, and temporarily suspended the acceptance of applications from securities firms to list new put warrants.
